summary.business: Established in 1967 and part of the Padmanabh Mafatlal Group, NFIL manufactures over 74 fluorochemical products spanning refrigeration gases (under the 'MAFRON' brand), inorganic and specialty fluorides, and CDMO (branded 'Navin Molecular') services for pharmaceutical and agrochemical customers. It operates one of India's largest integrated fluorochemical complexes, serving global life-science and crop-science majors, stainless-steel manufacturers and air-conditioner OEMs, with exports contributing ~67% of FY 2025-26 revenue across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia Pacific.

currentContext.strategies: Advancing complex fluorination chemistries, developing new molecules, and deepening long-term partnerships with global innovators remained central to strategy, supported by focused investments in Technology & Development, R&D and Business Development.|Actively progressing downstream value-accretive opportunities aimed at commercialising high-purity grades, including electronic-grade HF, and pursuing opportunities in the advanced materials space.|R&D centres at Surat, Dewas and Manchester focus on collaborating with clients to forge long-term partnerships in fluorine chemistry and niche chemistries, and on developing safe, cost-effective, scalable manufacturing processes.|Pursuing strategic growth opportunities in a disciplined fashion within a tight financial framework, with relentless management focus on manufacturing excellence — safe, compliant, reliable and efficient operations.|Increasing renewables footprint and reducing carbon intensity through long-term green-power sourcing arrangements.|Cross-functional teams driving efficient scale-up of processes and continuous improvement in productivity, quality and cost competitiveness to reinforce the Company's position as a reliable partner in high-value fluorochemicals.|The Board recommends dividend payments to shareholders out of annual profits, subject to Members' approval at the AGM, governed by the Companies Act, 2013 and the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy.
currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Board approved capex of ₹236.5 crores to add 15,000 MTPA equivalent HFC (R32 refrigerant) capacity, projected to generate peak annual revenue potential of ₹600-825 crores. The Company commissioned its AHF facility at Dahej (investment of ₹450 crores), a landmark step strengthening the fluorochemicals value chain, and is progressing downstream value-accretive opportunities to commercialise high-purity grades including electronic-grade HF, plus opportunities in the advanced materials space. In Specialty Chemicals, a ₹75 crore capital investment was progressed to debottleneck the Multi-Purpose Plant (MPP) at Dahej to support new molecule launches, alongside a strategic partnership with Chemours to manufacture Opteon (a two-phase immersion cooling fluid for hyperscale data-centre cooling), marking entry into the advanced materials space. In CDMO, the cGMP4 Phase 1 facility was commissioned, with supplies commencing from January 2026. At subsidiary Navin Fluorine Advanced Sciences Limited (NFASL), assets capitalised during FY26 amounted to ₹532.81 crores (including the recently commissioned AHF facility and maintenance/efficiency capex); in FY27 NFASL's capex will mainly go toward debottlenecking MPP facilities, expected to commission by Q3FY27. The Company also entered a Group Captive arrangement with Prozeal Green Power Eleven Private Limited to source renewable power under a long-term framework.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and global macro uncertainty
risks.note: The Board's Report explicitly notes results were achieved 'despite volatile geo political environment and challenging market dynamics'; the MD&A flags the Russia-Ukraine conflict and escalating Middle East tensions as disrupting supply chains, energy markets, trade routes and the purchase of critical inputs such as crude oil and LNG, and influencing capital flows.

risks.risk: Global trade policy and tariff uncertainty
risks.note: Sector-specific tariff adjustments and new bilateral trade agreements are flagged as adding complexity to the global trade environment; with exports spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia Pacific, the Company's international revenue is exposed to shifting tariff and trade-policy frameworks.

Key raw material costs moved in a mixed trend during the year, with sulphur prices rising while fluorspar, boric acid and chloroform prices declined y-o-y, indicating input-cost exposure that can pressure margins.

risks.risk: Global monetary tightening and financial market volatility
risks.note: The MD&A's macro outlook flags monetary tightening, elevated policy uncertainty and rising sovereign bond yields as downside risks to global growth, which can affect financing conditions and capital flows relevant to the Company's operations and expansion.

The Company derives a large share of turnover from exports across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia Pacific, making performance sensitive to demand, regulatory and policy conditions in those regions.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Specialty & agrochem CRAMS
themes.need: Custom-synthesis/CRAMS players with a dominant specialty-chemicals & agrochem-intermediate end-market are tied to the agrochem/specialty-chem capex cycle - not pharma APIs.
themes.driver: Specialty/agrochem custom-synthesis order wins tied to the agrochem/specialty-chem capex cycle.

It operates one of India's largest integrated fluorochemical complexes, serving global life-science and crop-science majors, stainless-steel manufacturers and air-conditioner OEMs, with exports contributing ~67% of FY 2025-26 revenue across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia Pacific.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global fluorochemicals market (5.03 million tonnes in 2025) expected to grow to 6.55 million tonnes by 2031, a 4.51% CAGR, driven by demand across electronics, EVs and refrigeration amid stringent environmental regulations.
- Refrigerants dominate global fluorochemicals demand (~55% of global revenue in 2025), with rising cold-storage and food-security infrastructure investment across India, Southeast Asia and the Gulf strengthening refrigerant consumption.
- Indian specialty chemicals industry (47% of India's chemical market) anticipated to grow at ~11% CAGR over the next five years, driven by automotive, pharmaceutical, agriculture and construction demand.
- Asia Pacific leads the global fluorochemicals market with 61.52% share, underpinned by expanding manufacturing and rising consumption in India.
- Global fluorochemicals supply chains are shifting focus from tariff absorption to cost optimisation, with companies reassessing supplier relationships, strengthening domestic capabilities and evaluating nearshoring.
- Growing demand from semiconductors, electronics, healthcare and aerospace applications is fuelling fluorochemicals sector growth, alongside cold-chain deployment, sustainability initiatives and regulatory compliance trends.
- HPP revenue growth driven by strong sales of the new R-32 capacity, orchid operations and improved pricing/mix; refrigerant gases business witnessed strong demand with improved pricing across products.
- Specialty Chemicals growth supported by ramp-up of new molecules, improved capacity utilisation across Dahej and Surat, and strong demand from global innovator customers.
- CDMO growth supported by scale-up of commercial molecules, strong execution of ongoing contracts, and increasing traction with global innovator customers.
- Key raw material costs moved in a mixed trend during the year: sulphur prices rose, while fluorspar, boric acid and chloroform prices declined y-o-y.
- Successful execution of pipeline molecules and safe ramp-up of the Nektar project were key drivers of Specialty Chemicals growth.
- CDMO business showed strong execution of ongoing contracts and increasing traction with global innovator customers.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 34.2% in Q4; 32.6% for FY26; 992 bps expansion; margin benefit from volume leverage (70%) and pricing (30%); currency tailwind largely offset by raw material inflation

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 the Board approved capex of ₹236.5 crores to add 15,000 MTPA equivalent HFC (R32 refrigerant) capacity, projected to generate peak annual revenue potential of ₹600-825 crores. The Company commissioned its AHF facility at Dahej (investment of ₹450 crores), a landmark step strengthening the fluorochemicals value chain, and is progressing downstream value-accretive opportunities to commercialise high-purity grades including electronic-grade HF, plus opportunities in the advanced materials space. In Specialty Chemicals, a ₹75 crore capital investment was progressed to debottleneck the Multi-Purpose Plant (MPP) at Dahej to support new molecule launches, alongside a strategic partnership with Chemours to manufacture Opteon (a two-phase immersion cooling fluid for hyperscale data-centre cooling), marking entry into the advanced materials space. In CDMO, the cGMP4 Phase 1 facility was commissioned, with supplies commencing from January 2026. At subsidiary Navin Fluorine Advanced Sciences Limited (NFASL), assets capitalised during FY26 amounted to ₹532.81 crores (including the recently commissioned AHF facility and maintenance/efficiency capex); in FY27 NFASL's capex will mainly go toward debottlenecking MPP facilities, expected to commission by Q3FY27. The Company also entered a Group Captive arrangement with Prozeal Green Power Eleven Private Limited to source renewable power under a long-term framework.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [R&D] Total R&D spend of ₹48.71 Crs in FY 2025-26 across three centres — Navin Research & Innovation Centre (Surat, Gujarat) and Navin Molecular R&D Centres (Dewas, MP and Runcorn, Manchester); the deck cites 65 chemists and 40 engineers in Technology and Design, and team sizes of 70 (Dewas R&D) and 18 (Runcorn MOL R&D).
